title: My Weirdly Good Lavender Tallow Balm Experiment
body:
Okay so my skin is a disaster. Like, a real piece of work. It’s this dry, flaky desert that also gets these angry red patches for no reason. I’m sitting here, it’s spring supposedly, but my face feels like old paper. The kind that cracks if you bend it. I’ve tried everything. The expensive stuff in the frosted glass jars, the drugstore lotions that smell like a chemical factory, the “clean” beauty oils that cost more than my electric bill. Nothing. My phone is buzzing on the couch next to me, battery at like 12%, and I’m just staring at this new jar of whipped tallow balm I got in the mail. Beef fat. For my face. It sounds insane. My friend sent me a link to this Etsy shop and I was bored one night at 11 PM and just clicked buy. The lavender one. For “calming.” I figured at worst, I’d have a very expensive candle.

Anyway. Here’s what happened.

## How Beef Tallow for Skin Even Became a Thing I Tried

My skin struggles are specific. It’s not just dry. It’s like… tight. And reactive. I used this fancy cream last winter, the one with the gold lid, and my cheeks turned the color of a stop sign for three days. So I got scared of everything. I was using just plain vaseline for a while which is, you know, fine. But it just sits there. It’s like putting plastic wrap on a plant. My skin would still be thirsty underneath all that goop. I saw people online talking about tallow skincare. Grass-fed beef tallow balm, whipped up. Saying it’s similar to the oils our skin already makes. I was skeptical. Very. The whole thing felt very frontier wife. But I was desperate. And curious. The “luxurious texture” description got me. I’m a sucker for texture.

So it arrived. Small jar. Made in France, which felt fancy for beef fat. I opened it. It didn’t look gross. It was just this off-white, kind of creamy looking stuff. I poked it. Weird. Not bad weird. It was solid but soft, like cold butter you can spread. I smelled it. Lavender? Yeah, but not the sharp, soapy kind. More like… the dried lavender my grandma had in her linen closet. Herbal. Quiet. Not perfumey. I was relieved. I hate strong smells. My cat was judging me from the doorway.

## What This Lavender Tallow Balm Actually Does

The first night I used it, I was tentative. I washed my face, patted it dry. My skin was doing that squeaky, tight thing it does. I scooped a tiny bit out with my finger. Rubbed it between my palms to warm it up. It melted fast. Like, instantly became an oil. I pressed it onto my face. Not rubbed, just pressed. And it… went in. It didn’t sit on top like vaseline. It didn’t disappear into nothing like those lotions. It just sort of sank in and left my skin feeling… not greasy. But not tight. Protected? I don’t know. It felt like my skin could finally breathe and be hydrated at the same time. A weird concept.

I started using it as my night cream. The lavender scent is supposed to be calming, sleep-promoting, all that. I’m not sure if it’s the scent or just the ritual, but my pre-bed anxiety scrolling did lessen. I’d put it on and just… go to bed. No fifteen-product routine. Just this one balm. I’d wake up and my face wasn’t an oil slick. It was just calm. The red patches on my cheeks? After about a week, they were less… loud. They faded to a pink whisper. The flakiness around my nose and eyebrows? Gone. Completely. My skin just felt even. Not perfect. Just even. Like it had finally stopped fighting me.

But the real test was my hands. I get these cracks in my knuckles every spring, no matter what. They hurt. I started using the leftover balm on my hands after doing my face. Just a dab. The cracks healed in, like, two days. I was shocked. This became my go-to for any dry spot. Elbows. Lips. A weird patch on my ankle. It just worked. It’s this natural moisturizer for dry, sensitive, reactive skin that actually absorbs. Doesn’t just coat.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of Tallow

So it’s been a month maybe. I’m looking for my keys, they’re under a magazine, and I catch my reflection in the microwave door. I stopped. My skin looked… good. Not “I just had a facial” good. Not filtered good. Just healthy. Like it belonged to me again. The constant tightness was gone. The foundation I used to wear to even out the redness just sits in my drawer. I don’t need it. I’m not saying I have perfect skin now. I still get a spot if I eat too much cheese. But the baseline? The baseline is just solid. Stable. It’s not a crisis anymore.

I told my mom about it. She has the same skin type—dry, sensitive, hates everything. She was horrified at first. “Beef fat? On your *face*?” But she tried it when she visited. She used it on her chapped lips and her winter-damaged cuticles. She stole my jar. I had to order another one. Now we both use it. I’m on my second jar from that little Etsy shop. I just set a reminder to order a third before I run out. It’s become that thing I don’t want to be without. Like my favorite mug. It’s simple. It works. I don’t have to think about it.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. Obviously. I already did.

Look, if you’re like me and your skin is sensitive and dry and just generally pissed off at the modern world, this might be worth a shot. The best tallow for that kind of reactive, delicate skin is one that’s simple. Just the tallow and maybe a scent you like. This lavender one is calming in a real way, not a marketing way. It’s not magic. It’s not going to make you look 20 again. But it might make your skin feel like it’s finally home. It did for me.

If you’re curious, I got mine from this small shop on Etsy. They just make the stuff. No big fancy brand. It feels like you found a secret.

Anyway. My coffee’s been cold for an hour. I should go heat it up.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yeah. The science-y reason is that it’s similar to the oils our skin already produces. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin something it already knows how to use. My dry, sensitive skin just ate it up.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this. But no, not for me. Because it absorbs so well, it doesn’t just block pores like some heavy creams can. It’s non-comedogenic. My skin actually feels clearer since using it, because it’s not freaking out from being dry.

**What does lavender tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like real lavender. Not laundry detergent. More herbal and earthy, like dried lavender in a old wooden drawer. It’s subtle. Fades pretty quick after you put it on. Just leaves a little calming vibe. It’s nice before bed.
